Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/23/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8188291
Permit API: 059-24414
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/23/2024
Comments: On 05/23/24 a routine complete inspection of the Gaydos 5 OG well site was conducted (CTS: TBD). Findings: -A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo #1). -The well and operator's information was displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo #2). -Some corrosion was observed on the well and production equipment (Photos #3-4).-A large area of distressed vegetation and exposed soil was observed inside and out of the earthen containment berm (Photo #5) -Elevated conductivity over 20mS was observed at multiple points both inside and out of the earthen containment berm (Photos #6-9). -Two possible aquatic features were observed on site at the time of inspection (Photos #12, 16). -Elevated conductivity was observed in both possible aquatic features (Photos #10-11, 15). -The leak appears to have originated from a crack in the lower portion of the poly tank (Photo #14).-The Department notified the operator and representatives from Diversified came to the site upon notification of the release. -The Department discovered the spill at 1:45pm and Diversified reported it to the Department at 2:50pm -The Department requests that the operator identify and delineate the two potential aquatic features. Violations of 78.54, 78.75(a), SWMA 301, and 78.66(b) for the release and failure to report prior to the Department finding the release.

Violation ID: 8263824
Permit API: 111-20223
Unconventional: No
County: Somerset
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/04/2026
Comments: On February 4, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management's Neilan 1 well located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039, where violations were issued for a release from a broken corroded pipe attached to the top of one of the production tanks on site. At the time of this inspection, the well site was snow covered, therefore, the vegetative cover of the well site, along with erosion and sedimentation issues throughout the well site and along the access road could not be assessed at this time.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead. Attached to this wellhead was a small metal production tanks, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this production tank either. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed some production equipment and a meter box on site, inside the meter box was production paper dated 10/27/2023. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this meter box or the production equipment attached to it. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right still had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time. During IR 4106039, the Department collected elevated soil conductivity readings at the base of the production tank with the broken piping. At the time of this inspection, the Department was unable to collect soil conductivity readings due to the ground being frozen. However visually, it did not appear that the release had been remediated yet due vegetation being overgrown around the production tank and release area.During IR 4106039, the Department requested the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of that inspection report. The written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, a plan for remediation of the spill or release, and how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requested the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon its receipt. To date, the Department has yet to receive the aforementioned documents. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from broken and corroded piping off of a production tank on site is remaining outstanding at this time.

At the time of this inspection, the well site was snow covered, therefore, the vegetative cover of the well site, along with erosion and sedimentation issues throughout the well site and along the access road could not be assessed at this time.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead. Attached to this wellhead was a small metal production tanks, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this production tank either. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed some production equipment and a meter box on site, inside the meter box was production paper dated 10/27/2023. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this meter box or the production equipment attached to it. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. properties.content:

Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Date: 10/03/2022
Comments: On October 3, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself and WQS Samuel Steingrabe. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3343707 where violations were outstanding due to deteriorated production fluid tanks that were discharging onto the ground, a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans. Also, no production reports have been submitted since 2014 per Department database. The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photos 2 and 3). No Emergency Response plans, or other required postings were onsite. The production fluid tanks onsite appear to have been replaced since IR 3343707 (see photos 5 and 15). Soil conductivity readings were taken underneath and around these tanks to determine whether petroleum products and/or production fluids were still present in the soil since IR 3343707. These readings were taken underneath the production fluid tank valves and in bare spots in their surrounding earthen berms. An additional reading was taken in a wet spot next to the tank farthest from the site entrance. The reading taken underneath the valve of the tank closest to the site entrance read 100 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken in the surrounding berm read 111 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). The soil conductivity reading taken underneath the valve of the tank farthest from the site entrance read 380 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). The one taken in a bare spot in the surrounding earthen berm read 640 Micro Siemens (see photo 11). The additional reading taken in the wet spot adjacent to the brine tank read 390 Micro Siemens (see photo 8). A background conductivity reading was taken in a well-vegetated spot at the well site entrance, reading 250 Micro Siemens see photo 16). No well tag was observed on the well or associated equipment with correct information (see photo 13), and the well API number was written on the meter box with sharpie. Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite (see photo 10). Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 14). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing. Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of October 3, 2022 and violations against the production fluid tanks have been corrected. However, outstanding violations that were continued in IR 3343707 due to production fluid discharge on the ground shall remain open since no NOV response or any information requested has been received from the operator to evaluate whether the release was remediated in accordance with chapter 78a. All other violations shall remain open as well since the rest of the site remains unchanged since IR 3343707.

It then ran around a freshwater drain pipe that was placed in at construction.The well is an open flowing well that appears to in production, with the valves opened. The well is plumbed to a gas separator and a 50 barrel poly tank within containment. Some stained soil is apparent between the separator and the containment, with elevated conductivity >1mS noted using a Soil EC meter probe. The total volume of brine leaked is likely close to the Operator's estimate of 30-35 gallons, with approximately 5-10 gallons being outside containment.The operator was called back. They said that they would have a contractor on site to dig up impacted soil early next week. Followup inspection will be dome then.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/29/2022 to BEECH RESOURCES LLC in Lycoming Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEECH RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/29/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 977323
Permit API: 081-21894
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/29/2022
Comments: On November 29, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the Beech Resources ISA Well Pad. At the time of inspection, Beech Resources was in stimulation operations of the recently drilled wells. An area of elevated soil conductivity was observed off the west end of the well pad in an area that was recently backfilled due to a developed erosion channel. The DEP screened the surrounding area and found the area of elevated conductivity to be approximately 180 ft. x 30 ft. This area encompasses the top of the well pad slope down past the compost filter socks in place and about 20 ft. past the compost filter sock. Soil conductivity in the area of impact ranged from 1,500 uS/cm to over range reading of the soil conductivity meter. The upper limit of the soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. Soil sample 0651-141 was collected from the area of impact. During the inspection, Don Stevenson with Beech Resources arrived onsite. DEP showed Mr. Stevenson where the area of elevated conductivity was found off the west end of the pad slope. While DEP was still onsite, Mr. Stevenson called to have an excavator sent to the well pad. Mr. Stevenson said Penn E and R was also called to schedule a time to delineate the spill. Due to the unknown volume of the spill, Beech Resources plans to clean up the area under the Act 2 remediation requirments. During the inspection, another area was observed off the southwest corner of the well pad where an erosion channel had formed at the top of the well pad slope and continued down past the compost filter sock off the permitted limit of disturbance. This area was also shown to Mr. Stevenson and he said that Beech Resources will dress up compost filter socks and backfill the channel that has formed.Much of the site has become vegetated. Temporary E and S controls are still in place and are in good condition except for the previously mentioned areas.The area of elevated levels of conductivity outside of containment off the well pad edge is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b). Additional violations could be assessed pending results from the soil sample collected. An erosion channel has formed at the top of the well pad slope and continues off the permitted limit of disturbance conveying sediment off the permitted site is an additional violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b) and Chapter 102.11(a)1.

Violation ID: 8258397
Permit API: 111-20223
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2025
Comments: On December 9, 2025, the Department conducted a Complaint Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County.At the time of this inspection, the well site was snow covered, therefore, the vegetative cover of the well site, along with erosion and sedimentation issues throughout the well site and along the access road could not be assessed at the time of this inspection. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a wellhead with a well tag fixed to it that had all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the wellhead. A small production tank was observed to be connected to the wellhead and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production tank either.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time. A conductivity meter was utilized to screen the area around the right production tank as well as utilized to collect a background soil conductivity reading of 0.234 mS taken upslope and adjacent to the well site. A soil conductivity readings of 1.285 mS was collected below a corroded pipe, and then readings of 0.0089 mS and 0.0694 mS were collected downslope of this area. The reading taken below the corroded pipe is elevated when compared to background, subjugating that a release likely occurred here. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the broken corroded pipe near the top of the production tank and for a release from corroded piping on the production tank.

The completions operations have ceased on Pad B and the snubbing rigs and their associated equipment have been removed from the pad. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad B. A representative from Creston Environmental was present on location as well. A crew was working on installing the GPUs on the pad. A vacuum truck was sucking up this fluid during this inspection. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up any elevated EC fluid found on the pad surface or during excavation on the pad. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) was empty during this inspection. A work crew was beginning to disassemble the MASS during this inspection. Another excavated area is to the southwest. According to Mr. Subra, EQT believes that the produced fluid that had been released to this area flowed along an area that had previously been excavated in association with a release that occurred during drilling operations on the well pad. Mr. Subra also said that the northwest area of the well pad where clamshell boxes had led to a release in the dancefloor area has been fully excavated. Additional excavation would still need to occur in the north central area of the well pad as well as in the northeast corner of the pad where the MASS still is present, he also stated. The lined sump remains at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel.Violations remain outstanding for the release of produced fluid to the northwest area of Pad B from clam shell boxes in the area of the dancefloor.

Inspection Date: 2020-01-27
Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Failure to immediately notify the Department of the release constitutes violations of 91.33(A) and 78.66(a). These violations have been closed as "unresolvable". Failure to have adequate secondary containment around the tanks constitutes a violation of 78.64(a). The existing containment structure was backfilled and did not have sufficient capacity to prevent the release from impacting waters of the Commonwealth. This constitutes a violation of 78.64(b). You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Roads. This Policy sets forth he procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Violation ID: 978345
Permit API: 015-23678
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2022
Comments: Site inspection conducted as a follow up to Notice of Violations (NOV) associated inspection report #3373528 dated 6/6/2022 and administrative inspection report #3386649 dated 7/5/2022. There are no Blackhill Energy personnel on site at time of inspection. Weather conditions are overcast and 31 degrees F. During this inspection, completions equipment is still attached to the wells drilled and stimulated during 2021. Two sand separators and a 500 barrel gas buster tank appear to be connected to gas wells (photo 2). Puddled fluid on site was screened using an Oakton PCTS 50 water conductivity meter and a Hanna Groline soil conductivity meter. While screening puddles around the well heads and 500 barrel gas buster frac tank, the Department observed fluid draining from the tank and releasing onto secondary containment (photo 3). The containment is open along the north end discharge port and puddled fluid on containment appears to be flowing off containment into the pad surface (photo 4). Water within containment is observed with conductivity reading 'Over Range' (>19.99 mS/cm). Puddles screened outside of containment are observed to range between 9.8 mS/cm near the north well head to 'Over Range' in a puddle next to the tank secondary containment. Sample 4406-018 collected at 11:45 from fluid puddled on pad rock surface between tank secondary containment and north-most gas well (photo 7). Sample will be analyzed using SAC 942. The Department notified Regina Logue, Blackhill Energy Environmental Manager, that the tank was leaking at 12:15. Ms. Logue indicated that Blackhill personnel were en route to the site and that Moody's Environmental was contracted to conduct site characterization. Violation noted for potential pollution. Additional violations may be issued pending results of water sample analysis. Previous NOV's associated with inspection report #3373528 dated 6/6/2022 and administrative inspection report #3386649 dated 7/5/2022 remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 10/13/2021
Violation Code: OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
Violation ID: 933247
Permit API: 051-23196
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2021
Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a complaint received by the Department of corroded production tanks and possible leak. Arrived on-site at approx. 1130 to conduct investigation. Well appeared equipped for production. No well label was observed on any of the production equipment on site. Recommend Operator affix permanent well label IAW the regulations. Well posting was present but has the wrong permit number on posting (Photo 3). Recommend Operator re-post with the appropriate and correct information for this well. Background conductance reading was taken in a field west of well pad (Photo 1). Conductance value in this location was 170 micro Siemens. Heavy corrosion was observed on production tanks. Holes have developed along the south and west sides of tank (Photos 2/4/5/8/9/10). A large hole (2'x2') has developed on the west side of tank. Production fluid/brine observed approx. 3" below large hole (Photo 5). Conductance of liquid in tank was 14,500 micro Siemens (Photo 6). Tank was located within earthen berm. Conductance readings were taken along the ground on the south and south-west sides of tank (Photos 4 & 8). Values were 3,740 & 4,510 micro Siemens respectively. These values were well above the background conductance reading and indicate a release of production fluid/brine onto the ground. Request Operator determine and provide quantity of release, the method how the quantity was determined, and the duration of the release. Recommend the Operator immediately remove all production fluid/brine from the production tank for proper disposal. It is also recommended that this production tank be removed and impacted soils beneath/adjacent to tank be delineated and areas impacted remediated. Production tank should be replaced once remediation is completed and confirmed by both the Operator and Department. NOTE: Conductance readings taken along the earthen berm were at background. It does not appear at this time that the release has migrated laterally. Violations are being cited related to the release of fluids to the ground and well label/posting. Pending Operator's response, additional violations may be cited.

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/12/2022
Comments: On May 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The small berm that was built to collect the seep was was dry and any water that is collected in that area is being vacuumed out. Upon arrival at the well pad, STL Resources was vacuuming water out of the northwest stormwater vault. The conductivity of the water that could not be vacuumed out was 2,500 uS/cm. About 18 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in this vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. STL Resources has back filled and rebuilt the excavated southwest and northwest infiltration berms that were impacted by the spill. DEP screened the water that had pooled up behind the northwest infiltration for conductivity and that resulted in 187 uS/cm. The conductivity of the small amount of water that pooled up behind the southwest infiltration berm was 40 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.1 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 188 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 196.2 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 59.9 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 44.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 133.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. During the inspection, STL Resources consultants were collecting soil samples from the well pad in a grid like pattern to delineate the area of the production fluid spill. Two of the holes that remained open had water pooled in them. Test Pit-209 which was about 7 yards to the north of the northwest stormwater vault had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water in test pit-209 was 2030 uS/cm and soil conductivity was difficult to measure to due the looseness of the soil in the hole. Soil sample 0651-117 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. Test Pit 211 which was about 15 yards to the north of 035-21325, had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water was 3,800 uS/cm and the soil conductivity was 1,180 uS/cm. Soil Sample 0651-118 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. DEP spoke with STL Resources Seth Rodriguez and he said that STL Resources is planning to hydroseed the site's earthen infiltration berms and parts of the site that are lacking vegetation. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 5, 6, and 8 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: On March 20, 2025, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Kriebel Natural Gas Co's RWS Development 001 Well located in Manor Borough, Westmoreland County in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release. Accompanying on today's inspection was Kriebel representative's Ben Dickun and Ronald Seich.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Dickun and Mr. Seich stated that the production tank on site had been emptied prior to our arrival on site and that they were going to install booms in the ditch that runs adjacent to the well site and terminates at a nearby stream downslope. The DEP inquired whether any other remediation efforts were going to be conducted while the DEP was on site or after the inspection, and Mr. Dickun stated that they were awaiting instruction from the DEP. At the time of this inspection, the DEP verbally recommended Kriebel promptly remediate the brine release in accordance with Act 2 protocol. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Other production equipment was observed on site and appeared to be charred, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. A production tank was observed on site with a large hole in its side, the tank had approximately 1-2 in of fluid pooled at the bottom of it, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production tank.During IR 3941481 and 3941519, the DEP collected several soil conductivity readings around the well site to determine the extent of the release and concluded that the brine release was contained to a ditch that runs alongside the well site edge and terminates just before a stream. No elevated conductivity readings were collected in the stream, therefore at the time of that inspection, it did not appear that there were any impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).At the time of this inspection, the DEP took a background soil conductivity upslope and away from the incident area (0.0833 mS), and then soil conductivity readings were taken within the ditch: Right by the production equipment (1.225 mS and 1.105 mS), right by a inlet that appeared to be plugged with rocks and plastic (1.165 mS), right by an outlet that appeared to be dry at the time of this inspection (0.828 mS), and then in the ditch leading up to where it terminates just before the stream (1.132 mS, 1.236 mS, and 1.348 mS,). Readings taken directly upslope of the ditch on both sides were comparable to the background reading, while readings taken inside the ditch were elevated, subjugating that the release still appears to be contained to the ditch. To determine whether the stream had become impacted from the brine release, at the time of this inspection, a soil conductivity readings was taken on the stream bank directly downslope of where the ditch terminates (0.593 mS), then a soil (0.402 mS) and fluid (0.459 mS) conductivity reading was taken in the stream directly downslope of where the ditch terminates and lastly, a fluid reading was taken upslope (0.527 mS) and downslope (0.524 mS) of this area. Based on the DEP's observations and these conductivity readings, it appears that the WOC at the time of this inspection remain unscathed from the brine release. The DEP recommends immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On January 8, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Yelenick 2 plugged well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following IR 4033716, where a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) was denied and violations were issued for failure to restore the well site within 9 months of plugging. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 10/24/2024, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 7/24/2025 in accordance with current regulations.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a mailbox and locked gate at the plugged well site's access road entrance. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed a Well Control and Disposal Plan as well as an Erosion and Sediment Control Plan. The beginning portion of the access road was observed to be graveled, however the remaining portion of the access road was observed to be restored and exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth.Upon inspection of the plugged well site, the Department observed the site to be exhibiting 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. Compost Filter Sock was observed to be installed on site as well as a pipeline riser. According to the Operator NOV response (documented in IR 4048289) the pipeline riser is still in use. At the time of this inspection no surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed to be coming from the pipeline riser or the approximate coordinate location of the plugged well. Based on today's inspection, it appears that the well site and access road is still not fully restored, therefore violations are being continued for failure to restore the well site and access road within 9 months of plugging.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an Inspection App IT error.

Inspection Date: 10/13/2022
Comments: On October 13, 2022, the Department conducted a Routine inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself, ET Marcella Dantzler, those listed from the SWDO OG Team, and EQT representatives Joe Eversman and Logan Dominick.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road, and was not obstructed by vegetation (see photo 2). The ER and PPC plans were not available immediately upon arrival (see photo 3). A site safety and environmental plan was found in the office onsite. A PPC plan was also in the office, but missing required components. Neither the secondary containment inspection records nor the well permit were available onsite when requested. A sediment basin was observed along the left side of the access road, looking towards the pad. A forebay cleanout was observed on the opposite side, with a culvert connecting them under the access road (see photo 5). Cattails were observed in the sediment basin. A further review will be conducted to ensure that they are part of the PCSM plan. A soil stockpile was observed along the left side of the access road, immediately before entering the pad (see photo 6). The operator was actively drilling onsite. This is the first well being drilled. The operator intends to drill 4 wells total. A destabilized area of soil was discovered behind the sound wall on the eastern side of the well pad (see photo 15). Preexisting metal and brick was observed outside of the LOD at this location, as was noted in the site E and S plans (see photo 16). A tear in the rig site containment was observed at the southern side of the pad. This was brought to Mr. Eversman's attention, who immediately called in a crew to repair it (see photo 12). Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. He also stated that the site ERP and PPC plans had previously been placed into the mailboxes attached to the Act 9 sign, and that they were likely removed by a nuisance third party.Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the aforementioned unstable soil spot behind the sound wall is re-stabilized. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.

Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. He also stated that the site ERP and PPC plans had previously been placed into the mailboxes attached to the Act 9 sign, and that they were likely removed by a nuisance third party.Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the aforementioned unstable soil spot behind the sound wall is re-stabilized. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 12/08/2025
Comments: On 12/08/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of Seneca Resources Co. LLCs DCNR 007 Pad L multi-well pad located in Shippen Township, Tioga County. Upon arrival to the site at 1130 hours, weather was 12F and partly cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).This inspection was conducted in response to a spill reported by Seneca on 12/07/2025 at 1015 hours which details a 10 gallon release of coolant from a HydroEdge truck due to a hose clamp malfunction (CID #393975). This spill was immediately cleaned up with booms and absorbent materials and the impacted pad materials were scraped and removed (photos #2-4). These impacted materials were placed in a 55 gallon drum for disposal and are temporarily being held in secondary containment until disposal occurs (photo #5).No fluids were observed on the pad surface.There are 5 wells currently undergoing active stimulation operations (photo #6). All stimulation activities are taking place on rig matting which serves as a pad-wide containment system; the rig matting appears to be functioning as intended (photo #7). Numerous temporary storage tanks were observed in tertiary containment, these tanks hold produced fluids for stimulation (photos #8 and 9). Sand storage tanks were also observed on the rig matting (photo #10). The chemical storage areas are stationed on the rig matting and these areas appear to be tidy and free from any spills or releases (photos #11 and 12).Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed due to snow cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. An E and S inspection log is available for review and up to date (photo #13). Numerous infiltration berms serve as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls (photos #14-21). No stormwater was observed in the PCSM controls and they held snow at the time of this inspection.Due to the release of 10 gallons of coolant from a HydroEdge truck onto the pad surface, a violation of 35 P.S. 691.402(b) is cited against API #117-22218; however, due to the immediate cleanup and remediation of the impacted area, this violation is noted as immediately corrected.I departed the site at 1230 hours.
